blocks: Chemical Etching For Architecture

Trade Etching Direct are the UK's leading specialists in chemical etching for architecture. By combining our expertise and years of experience in chemical etching and metal patination, we offer a near limitless range of unique custom architectural metal surfaces. We can etch a vast range of metals, in sheets up to 2500mm x 1250mm. From vectored artwork, we can etch virtually any shape, pattern, logo, or image desired, producing genuinely unique architectural metal designs. We expertly apply a wide range of patina finishes to create bespoke designs. Materials we work with include Brass, Bronze, Rimex Metals®, Steel (stainless, mirrored, & Corten), Aluminium, Copper, and more. In addition to etching and patination, our in-house services include CNC routing, laser cutting, and digital printing.
The Grand Lobby - Cunard's Queen Anne

Trade Etching Direct etched and patinated the 97 brass panels that form Canadian artist Ian Kirkpatrick's stunning mural 'A Cunard Journey' onboard Cunard’s Queen Anne. ‘A Cunard Journey’ is an Art Deco celebration of the golden age of liner travel, situated in the heart of Queen Anne’s Grand Lobby. Covering an area of 391 sq. m, the highly detailed etched panels were bent and assembled to create an impressive lenticular centerpiece. This dynamic installation comes to life, showcasing three distinct artworks as guests traverse the space. Lighting effects throughout the day bring out different qualities in the brass material, which appears light and welcoming in the morning, gradually becoming dimmer and more glamorous in the evening.

Chemical etching is a method of engraving that uses a high pressure, temperature regulated, chemical spray to remove material to create a permanent etched image or shape in metal. A UV sensitive resist is then applied to the surface of the material and is selectively removed using a photographic process, to expose the areas to be etched. This process allows for reproduction of exceptionally detailed artwork. There is no heat distortion as associated with laser processing, and no tool wear, as with mechanical engraving methods. In the etching process the material is dissolved atom by atom, producing a smooth burr free finish and leaving the material grain structure unaffected.

The British Sign Awards shine a light on British sign makers and provide a showcase for the ‘Best of British’. Since they were launched in 2013, the Awards have celebrated some truly remarkable achievements that have demonstrated that the skills and creativity of British sign businesses is world class. The awards are open to all UK-based sign businesses. The Craftsman award is designed to recognise traditional sign making skills. Entries can be complete signs created using traditional methods or can be signs produced using modern techniques but which include a hand-crafted element.

Trade Etching Direct produced a total of 16 trophies, each one made up of ten components. The front panel was produced from laser-cut 3mm brushed stainless steel , etched and digitally printed with the Awards logo, category and winner’s details and individual sponsor logo; the back panel consisted of 3mm laser cut, patinated brass, reverse etched with the logo of ISA-UK, hosts for the event. TED incorporated re-chargeable internal LED illumination to create an edge-lit effect.

blocks: Innovative Metal Etching & Finishing Solutions for Custom Signage and Architectural Applications

Welcome to the Concepts section of Trade Etching Direct, where we showcase our latest ideas and innovations in metal etching and finishing. As a leader in the UK sign industry, we are dedicated to pushing the boundaries of what’s possible, providing our customers with unique and exciting design options. This section serves as a creative space where we share the new possibilities we’re exploring in metal etching. Whether it's intricate patterns, innovative finishes, or bold new applications, our goal is to inspire and inform our customers about the extensive capabilities at their disposal. Explore these concepts to see how our advanced techniques can bring your projects to life in ways you might not have imagined.
Laser cut and reverse etched celtic cross

A laser cut 3mm mirror stainless Celtic cross, deep reverse etched to a depth of 0.8mm with a smooth, uniform etched surface. This project showcases the possibilities of combining laser cutting with deep etching, allowing for both intricate design and durable craftsmanship. The precision of laser cutting paired with the depth and detail of etching opens up endless creative possibilities for custom projects like this.
Penrose Tile Patina

Introducing a concept Penrose tile patina finish, combining several different patina finishes into brass to highlight the intricate and mesmerizing patterns of Penrose tiles. Discovered by the renowned British physicist Sir Roger Penrose,  Penrose tiles are a set of tiles that can cover a plane in an aperiodic manner, ensuring that no part of the tiling repeats exactly, regardless of the size of the area covered, demonstrating the beauty of mathematical tiling. Sir Roger Penrose is celebrated for his contributions to mathematics and physics, including his work on black holes, general relativity, and the Penrose-Hawking singularity theorems. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2020 for his discoveries in the field of black hole formation and structure. His work continues to inspire scientists and mathematicians around the world.
Peacock Patina Finish

Some new signage concepts featuring etched and patinated brass. These designs are inspired by the elegance and beauty of peacocks, aiming to create a luxurious and distinctive look. The combination of detailed etching and rich patina brings depth and character to each piece.
4mm Etched Bronze With Patina

17 etched and patinated bronze plaques, each measuring 1400x920mm and 4mm thick, for the Garda Monument of Remembrance at Phoenix Park, Dublin. This project showcases our large etching capabilities. The Garda Monument of Remembrance commemorates the lives and service of all Garda personnel – members of An Garda Síochána and Garda staff - who died whilst in service since the organisation’s founding in 1922. The refurbished Garda Monument of Remembrance features the names of over 1,800 Garda personnel who died whilst in service over the last 100 years
5mm Reverse Etched Brass with Patina

Reverse etched 5mm brass piece with a patina finish. The intricate detailing and elegant craftsmanship truly stand out. This unique combination of brass and patina is perfect for creating sophisticated and eye-catching signage.
Laser Cut 3mm Polished Brass With Patina
A blend of clean modern design with aged, textured elements. Check out the close-up shots for more detail.

Typical materials requested by our customers include: ◈ Stainless steel ◈ Brass ◈ Bronze ◈ Copper ◈ Nickel ◈ Zinc ◈ Aluminium ◈ Mild steel ◈ Rimex Metals® incl T22™ range Other materials are available on request. Applications

Typical applications for chemical etching include: ◈ Hotel & office signage ◈ Wayfinding  signage ◈ Industrial nameplates & labels ◈ Identification products ◈ Architectural panels ◈ Plaques & memorials ◈ Interpretation boards ◈ Corporate awards ◈ Safety & compliance signs ◈ Promotional items ◈ Thin metal components
What is chemical etching?

Chemical etching is a multistage photo-lithographic process.  The metal is first cleaned and then laminated with a UV sensitive photoresist film. A photo tool containing the desired artwork is placed on top of the laminated material. It is then exposed to UV light. The UV light passes through the clear areas of the photo tool hardening the laminated film. The sheet is then chemically developed to wash away the unexposed photoresist leaving a very precise mask of hardened photoresist behind. The material is placed in the etching machine where is it sprayed with a high pressure temperature regulated chemical  spray (most commonly Ferric Chloride).  The solution etches away the unprotected portions of the material to reproduce the desired image. The chemical spray dissolves the material atom by atom for a smooth burr free finish. In the final stage the photoresist is stripped away leaving the material ready for any post etching processes required.

Chemical Milling

Chemical milling is a process used to produce complex thin metal components out of sheet metal. In the milling process artwork is applied to both sides of the material and is etched from top and bottom simultaneously. It is a flexible process with low tooling costs that produces burr-free, stress-free parts

title: Etched metal signage for theme parks, TV & film props
description: Etched metal signage for theme parks, TV & film props
blocks: Signage for theme parks, film & TV props

In the realm of theme parks and immersive attractions, every detail contributes to the magic. Etched metal signage offers an unparalleled combination of durability and aesthetic finesse, essential for creating believable and captivating environments. Imagine intricately etched brass plaques adorning fantastical shopfronts, weathered steel directional signs guiding adventurers through mystical lands, or robust control panel overlays for interactive exhibits. Unlike printed or painted alternatives, the deep-etched details in materials like stainless steel, brass, or even copper, withstand the elements and high footfall, ensuring that the story and atmosphere remain intact for years. This permanence and tactile quality lend an air of authenticity that truly transports guests, making etched metal the ideal choice for everything from ride warnings and informational displays to thematic branding and decorative elements that define a unique park experience.
Bringing Detail to Life: Film & Television Props

For film and television productions, authenticity in props can make or break a scene. Etched metal signage and components provide a level of detail and realism that is often crucial for close-ups and creating a believable diegetic world. Consider custom-etched dog tags for a period war film, futuristic data plaques for a sci-fi epic, or ornate, aged metal labels for mysterious artifacts in a fantasy series. The ability to precisely replicate intricate designs, logos, fictional languages, or technical schematics onto various metals allows prop masters to achieve a high degree of accuracy and visual storytelling. Furthermore, the inherent robustness of etched metal means props can endure the rigours of production, from on-set handling to multiple takes, maintaining their integrity and appearance throughout the filming process
Versatility in Design & Application

The versatility of etched metal extends beyond simple signage. For both theme parks and production sets, this technique can be applied to create bespoke control panels with intricate markings, custom-branded metal components for machinery or vehicles, detailed plaques for set dressing, or even unique, collectible merchandise. The etching process allows for fine lines, detailed graphics, and various textural finishes, from brushed and polished to deliberately aged or patinated effects. This adaptability ensures that whether the requirement is for a sleek, modern aesthetic or a rustic, time-worn look, etched metal can be tailored to perfectly match the creative vision, adding a layer of sophistication and tangible quality that enhances the overall production value and immersive experience.
